Diego —

Heads-up: Blackbridge (Avery Nash) just signaled they want a dedicated pool for Q4 POC with a production ramp in Q1. They asked for a standby/soft-commit option so they can close procurement quickly. Can you run a quick availability scan and give me two proposals: (A) a 60-day standby (no charge until commit) with node count and expected latency profile; (B) a refundable escrow-style reserve with partial commit pricing. Need something to share with procurement by EOD tomorrow.

Attached the deal summary and their original SOW for context.

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>

Date: 2029-06-12T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Blackbridge late-stage — availability scan + proposed standby options

Marissa —

Ran a capacity sweep across US-west and US-east GPU pools. Summary below (preliminary):

Option A — 60-day standby (no billing until activation)
- Suggested config: 8x A100-80GB equivalent (dedicated pool), average concurrent requests 120 qps with batching targets; predicted p95 token latency ~170ms for gen-16k workloads.
- Risk: causes ~4% utilization displacement on existing thin-margin committed customers for the duration; we can mitigate with short horizon autoscale and strict burst policy.
- Ops ask: require a manual global capacity hold and playbook for preemption windows.

Option B — Refundable escrow reserve (partial billing at reduced rate)
- Suggested config: 6x A100-80GB equivalent reserved; 30% refundable credit on monthly commit if they pull out before activation.
- Advantage: preserves lane for them without full displacement; billing covers NRE for nodal priming.

Attachments: detailed node mapping and availability matrix. Priyom — can you granularize the latency numbers by model bucket (base/quantized/4-bit) and add expected cost delta vs. hosted API? Rishi — please flag any SLA exceptions if we do manual hold in US-west.

I'll draft a short customer-facing note once we align internally.

- Diego
Director, Infrastructure Operations
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: gpu_availability_scan_q2_2029.xlsx (XLSX, 95KB)]

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>

Date: 2029-06-13T08:46:00-07:00
Subject: Proposal: standby reserve vs refundable escrow — Blackbridge POC path

Avery / Procurement team —

Thanks again for the productive call. Per Marissa's ask and our internal scan, attached are two operational paths we recommend so Blackbridge can secure dedicated capacity for the Q4 PoC while keeping procurement flexibility:

1) 60-day Standby (no billing until activation)
- Capacity: 8 dedicated A100-80GB class nodes reserved in US-west region.
- Activation: customer can trigger activation with 7 days' notice; we guarantee node availability during the standby period except during declared emergency maintenance windows.
- SLA: standard Redwood Dedicated SLA applies post-activation. Standby period has a best-effort availability assurance (detailed in attachment).

2) Refundable Escrow Reserve
- Capacity: 6 dedicated nodes reserved.
- Billing: 30% of full reserved price billed monthly as a refundable credit; refunded pro-rata if the reservation is not activated within 90 days.
- Benefit: smaller upfront commitment, preserves capacity without full financial exposure.

Next steps if you'd like to proceed: (1) indicate preferred option and region; (2) we’ll produce an MOU for a standby/escrow and hand off to legal; (3) if Option A is chosen, Ops will run final node-lock and blackout windows.

Attachments: one-page summary + technical appendix.

Best,
Diego
Director, Infrastructure Operations
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: standby_mou_blackbridge_v1.docx (DOCX, 12KB)]

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Procurement has two quick questions before we move to an MOU: (1) can you guarantee no capacity displacement for our activation window (we need consistent latency during POC) and (2) is the refundable escrow refundable on day 1 if we decide to go hosted instead? Our CFO is sensitive to any sunk costs.

Prefer Option B if refund is available early; otherwise we may take Option A but ask for a 5-day activation SLA.

Thanks —

Subject: Re: Proposal: standby reserve vs refundable escrow — Blackbridge POC path

Avery / Team —

Short answers to your questions:
(1) Guarantee on zero displacement: we cannot offer an absolute zero-displacement guarantee for best-effort standby; however, for the duration of a binding escrow reserve (Option B) we can contractually reserve the nodes and include an SLA credit for material latency deviations. If you require firm latency SLAs from day 1, Option B (refundable escrow) is the correct path.

(2) Refundability timing: escrow refunds are pro-rata and can be structured to allow full refund if Blackbridge opts into hosted API before activation (we will reflect that in the MOU language). There will be a 5-day processing window for refunds to clear.

Given your CFO note, I recommend Option B with explicit refund-on-hosted clause and a 5-day activation SLA written into the MOU. Marissa — please confirm and loop Legal so we can fast-track the MOU. Priyom / Rishi — can you prep the final SLO wording and the cost delta appendix for the doc?

Diego
